metadata.notes: DeepSeek Harness /clear rotates the live TUI to a fresh durable session UUID, and irrlicht can retire the prior row when the new session claims the same PID.

assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: full
driver_capability: ready

## Agent capability

The installed DeepSeek Harness TUI 0.8.1 exposes `/clear` as `Clear the screen and start a new session`. Its command dispatcher calls `actions.clear()`. The implementation waits for the current agent to become idle, flushes and disposes it, and then calls `attachSession(undefined)`. That fresh attach creates `session-${randomUUID()}`. The TUI process remains alive. The agent therefore implements the scenario's in-process session reset and produces a distinct durable session ID.

## Daemon capability

The DSH adapter watches every highest-generation `session.vN.jsonl.zstd` below the DSH sessions root. It derives the daemon ID from the `session-<uuid>` directory. The new `/clear` transcript therefore appears as a new session row. The adapter binds a real session to the process that holds its sibling `session.lock` open. Because `/clear` keeps the TUI process alive, the post-reset session claims the same PID as the pre-reset session. `PIDManager.HandlePIDAssigned` records `pid_discovered`, finds the prior non-subagent holder of that PID, records `transcript_removed` for the old ID, deletes the old row, and broadcasts the deletion. This is the exact observable required by `Old session disappears`.

The DSH parser maps `turn/start` to working and a completed `turn/end` to the authoritative `turn_done` signal. Existing DSH recordings prove a real UUID session binds through `session.lock` and completes a tool-free working-to-ready turn. The reset-specific end-to-end timing remains provisional until `record`, but every required signal has a concrete local trace and daemon path.

## Driver capability and recipe

The interactive driver declares and implements `send`, `wait_turn`, `sleep`, and `reset_session`. `reset_session` saves the old transcript slot, reuses the live tmux pane and cwd in a new slot, sends `/clear`, and resolves a post-marker transcript with a fresh UUID. The shared contract writer emits both slots through `session.uuids` and `transcript.paths`, so curation keeps both halves of the reset arc.

The recipe uses 10 seconds before reset, 8 seconds after reset, and 8 seconds after the second turn. These values cover the longest corresponding sibling delays. The 600-second budget covers two measured local qwen turns plus reset and settle time. Both prompts demand exact terminal tokens and forbid tools.

The observation vector pins `qwen/qwen3.5-9b` because the driver selects it and existing DSH transcripts confirm that model. It requires non-zero tokens. It does not require non-zero cost because the local LM Studio model has no applicable priced provider record.
caveats: Vacuous-pass condition: an unrelated second DSH session could satisfy the new-session phases without proving /clear if it entered the curated set. The load-bearing controls are the driver's fresh per-run cwd, its post-reset marker, and the aligned two-entry session.uuids/transcript.paths contract. Record must confirm that the two durable session headers have the same cwd and distinct IDs.
Load-bearing environment precondition: LM Studio must listen at http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1 with qwen/qwen3.5-9b loaded. The driver selects that endpoint and model through its temporary patch.

The old-row removal verdict is source-backed but provisional for reset timing. Record must observe the post-reset session binding to the same PID and the old session's transcript_removed event after that binding.

A separate concurrent two-process DSH recording exposed a wrong transcript_path on one teardown event. This reset spec matches old-row removal by session ID and also asserts the two durable transcript IDs. Record must report any reset-path identity crossover instead of weakening the phase.

The DSH file watcher can emit a short transcript_removed/transcript_new pair for the same UUID while the compressed file is replaced. The phase chain pins reset to a different session ID, so that same-ID replacement cannot satisfy the reset assertion.
The local model cost is expected to remain zero. The spec asserts the configured model and non-zero tokens, not non-zero cost.

sources.note: Installed TUI 0.8.1 documentation defines /clear as flushing the current session and starting a new one.
The shipped command registry exposes /clear and dispatches it to actions.clear().
clearSession flushes and disposes the old agent, then attachSession(undefined) creates session-${randomUUID()} while the TUI process remains alive.
FilesUnderRoot keys rows by the session UUID directory, DiscoverPID uses the sibling session.lock writer, and the parser maps explicit DSH turn boundaries.
HandlePIDAssigned and cleanupStalePIDHolders record transcript_removed and delete the prior non-subagent holder when a new session claims the same PID.
Implements reset_session through /clear, resolves a fresh post-marker transcript slot, and implements every other recipe primitive.
Slot bookkeeping preserves the old and new transcript identities, and the contract writer emits both to curation.
Measured DSH lifecycle: a real UUID session appears in ready, binds a positive PID through session.lock, runs working to ready, and is removed on process exit.
Measured DSH turn carries qwen/qwen3.5-9b, non-zero usage, a literal tool-free assistant reply, and a completed durable turn boundary.
Separate concurrent-session evidence for the narrow teardown transcript-path caveat; the reset recording must check identity rather than assume it.

preconditions: dsh 0.1.5-rc.2 or newer is on PATH and the community tui profile with @tomowang/dsh-tui 0.8.1 or newer is installed under the active DSH home
LM Studio is listening at http://127.0.0.1:1234/v1 with qwen/qwen3.5-9b loaded
tmux, zstd, and jq are on PATH
irrlichd is recording with the DeepSeek Harness transcript permission granted
setup: The driver creates a fresh per-run cwd and launches one DSH TUI in tmux.
A temporary patch selects LM Studio and qwen/qwen3.5-9b without modifying the installed profile.
The reset step preserves the old transcript slot, sends /clear in the live TUI, and resolves a distinct post-marker transcript in the same cwd.

script.text: Do not use tools. Reply with exactly this token and nothing else: BEFORE-RESET
Do not use tools. Reply with exactly this token and nothing else: AFTER-RESET

verify: session.uuids and transcript.paths contain two aligned, distinct DSH session UUIDs
both compressed transcript headers contain the same fresh per-run cwd and distinct IDs
the pre-reset session completes one ready to working to ready turn and contains the exact BEFORE-RESET reply
after /clear, a different session appears in ready and binds to the same live TUI PID
the pre-reset session emits transcript_removed and leaves the dashboard after the new session claims that PID
the post-reset session completes one ready to working to ready turn and contains the exact AFTER-RESET reply
neither transcript contains a tool call or a waiting transition
the recording reports qwen/qwen3.5-9b and non-zero tokens
recipe.scope_note: Uses the longest sibling timing at each reset landmark: 10 seconds before reset, 8 seconds after reset, and an 8-second final settle. DSH creates the post-reset transcript immediately, but the after-reset delay also gives irrlicht time to bind the same PID and retire the old row before the second turn starts.
